segments.caption: The video opens with a title card reading "Beekeeping 101," introducing the subject. It then cuts to an outdoor scene where an older man, identified by a lower-third graphic as Dave Stokesberry, a beekeeper, is shown in profile. He is wearing a cap and glasses and appears to be speaking, likely offering introductory advice or a personal account about beekeeping, setting the stage for an educational segment.

An older man, identified as beekeeper Dave Stokesberry, walks purposefully through his backyard toward his beehives, which are visible on the path. The scene is set on a sunny day in a residential yard with a white car and a wooden fence in the background.

An elderly beekeeper in a maroon cap and overalls walks through his backyard apiary in Puyallup, Washington, approaching his beehives. He bends over and carefully handles a jar, likely containing honey or a beekeeping tool, as he tends to his hives on a sunny day, surrounded by a wooden fence and lush greenery.

An older beekeeper, wearing a purple cap and overalls, is actively managing his apiary in a sunny backyard in Puyallup, Washington. He is shown inspecting and opening various wooden beehives, carefully examining the interior frames, which are covered in bees and honeycomb, as part of his routine beekeeping activities.

A beekeeper carefully lifts the lid of a beehive, revealing a frame densely populated with bees and honeycomb, then gently extracts the frame to inspect the hive’s activity in a sunlit outdoor setting.
A beekeeper lifts a screened frame from a hive, revealing a bustling colony of bees actively moving over a honeycomb filled with golden honey, set against a backdrop of a sunny, grassy yard.

An elderly beekeeper, wearing a cap and glasses, is shown tending to his hives in a sunny backyard. He carefully inspects a honeycomb frame filled with bees and developing honey, demonstrating his hands-on care for his apiary.

An older beekeeper, wearing a plaid shirt and a purple cap, carefully holds up a honeycomb frame teeming with bees in his backyard garden. The close-up shots reveal the bees actively moving across the hexagonal cells, some appearing to be working on the comb while others cluster around. The man, likely inspecting the hive's health or progress, looks down at the frame with focused attention, surrounded by green grass, a wooden fence, and flowering plants under bright daylight

An elderly man in a maroon cap and glasses stands in his sunny backyard garden, speaking to the camera while tending to his bees. The camera briefly zooms in on a wooden beehive where several bees are actively moving, before returning to the man as he continues his conversation, with a wooden fence and lush greenery forming the backdrop.

An elderly beekeeper, Dave Stokesberry, stands in his sunny backyard garden, speaking to the camera. The scene cuts to a close-up of numerous bees actively crawling and flying around the entrance of a wooden beehive, highlighting the core activity of his beekeeping operation.
A beekeeper at Stokesberry Hives in Puyallup, Washington, is shown tending to his beehives and proudly displaying a jar of his freshly harvested honey.
An older man outdoors holds up a jar of honey, then opens it to show the thick, golden liquid dripping from the lid onto a white surface, demonstrating its quality and viscosity.

An elderly man, wearing glasses and a purple cap, carefully compares a sample of dark liquid on a white dish against the contents of a glass jar, then examines a small, mesh-covered metal object, likely part of a homemade or vintage device, in his workshop.

An elderly beekeeper, wearing a purple cap and glasses, is shown in his apiary, carefully tending to his hives and handling jars of honey, showcasing his dedicated work in beekeeping and honey production.

A beekeeper is shown tending to a beehive in a backyard setting, lifting lids to inspect the frames teeming with bees. The segment concludes with a text overlay highlighting honey’s remarkable longevity and purity.

The video presents a series of static text screens on a black background, serving as an informational and credit sequence. The first screen states that honey is one of the purest foods ever known, having remained so for at least 9,000 years. The second screen credits Dave, his friends, and neighbors for their knowledge or involvement, likely in relation to the honey theme. The final screen credits Jack D. Hubbard for cinematography.
